title: the Sri Yantra
hook: a flat map becomes a mountain: the Sri Yantra raised
tomorrow: what if the yantra were drawn on the one who reads it?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Sri Yantra read two ways: outward as srishti, creation, and inward as samhara, the way back. Today the week comes back, and the drawing stands up.
screen: `A ROAD THAT WORKS FROM EITHER END.`

segments.voice: On a hiking map, a mountain is just a few rings of lines on flat paper. Then the trail starts, and those rings turn into a climb that burns your legs. Lift the Sri Yantra the same way. Raise the center. Lift the triangles above the petals, the petals above the rings, until the whole thing rises to a peak with the bindu at the top. It's still the Sri Yantra. It has just stopped lying flat.
screen: `RINGS ON A HIKING MAP.` → `RAISE THE CENTER.` → `THE YANTRA STANDS UP.`

segments.voice: This raised form has a name: the Meru, after the great mountain that Hindu stories place at the center of the world. Some worshippers keep a Meru, cast in metal or carved in stone, on a home altar or in a temple shrine, and it receives worship just as the flat yantra does. Lineages differ on which form they prefer. What the Meru makes plain is something the flat drawing only hints at: yesterday's inward road is also an upward climb. To go in toward the point is to go up toward the summit. The outer square is the ground you start from; the layers are the slopes. Now look back down the mountain at the week. A muddy pond, and a lotus opening clean. Nine triangles that won't come apart. A dot where the Goddess sits, and two loving answers about who walks all the way in. Red powder, edge first. One short word, Sri, at the top of the page. And a road that works from either end. All of it, now, a small hill on a shelf.
screen: `MERU: THE YANTRA AS A MOUNTAIN.` · `GOING IN IS GOING UP.` · `THE WEEK, FROM THE SUMMIT.` · then, large: `THE SAME MAP, AS A MOUNTAIN.`

segments.voice: Sit tall, like a small mountain: a wide, steady base, the spine rising, the crown of the head light. Let the breath move on its own, slow and unforced. Rest your attention at the top of your head, the summit, and stay there, the way a peak stays put while weather passes over it.
The Sri Yantra, raised: the Meru, a mountain form of the same diagram, where going in is going up.
One line to keep: the Sri Yantra, the same map drawn as a mountain. A week, climbed.
